interpretations.statement: Unreviewed interpretation: For a distributor promoting products to a client, the quoted paragraph 3.11 gift prohibition applies when the offered item is a gift, is not a discount of fees or charges, and the promotion is linked to either a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product.

assumptions: The assessed actor is a distributor promoting products to a client, as stipulated in the selected question.
The supplied classifications are independent evidence inputs; no truth values are inferred.
The purpose sentence explains the prohibition without imposing a separate test of actual investor distraction.
The evaluation concerns the quoted retained text only and does not decide temporal applicability.

citations.quote: distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.
The purpose of the requirement is to avoid the use of gifts to distract investors from the features and risks of a particular product.
such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses
then such gifts will be bound by this requirement as investors may be distracted from the unique features and risks of such particular funds3.

reading.distinction: The prohibition applies to a gift linked to either a specific product or a product type, subject to the discount exception. The stated risk of distraction supplies a rationale, not an additional factual condition. A competing actual-distraction test lacks sufficient textual support. The strongest unresolved source uncertainty is the omitted footnote.
